s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent lesion of the nasal vestibule with local invasion
salient_findings: Recurrent lesion of the right nasal vestibule mucosa
Tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
Never-smoker
Initial lesion biopsied 5 years prior
Initial biopsy reported as solid and cystic hidradenoma
p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative on initial biopsy
Lesion recurred 8 months prior to presentation
Second excision showed p63 positive and p16 negative with positive margins
Enlarged, firm right ala on examination
Tumor visualized within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
Imaging showed thicker right ala compared to the left ala

raw.syndrome_frame: Recurrent lesion of the nasal vestibule with local invasion
salient_findings: Recurrent lesion of the right nasal vestibule mucosa
Tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
Never-smoker
Initial lesion biopsied 5 years prior
Initial biopsy reported as solid and cystic hidradenoma
p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative on initial biopsy
Lesion recurred 8 months prior to presentation
Second excision showed p63 positive and p16 negative with positive margins
Enlarged, firm right ala on examination
Tumor visualized within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
Imaging showed thicker right ala compared to the left ala

raw.rationale: The patient's lesion showed a downward papillomatous proliferation of small, uniform, slightly atypical keratinocytes within loose stroma, which is consistent with verrucous carcinoma. The initial biopsy reported a solid and cystic hidradenoma, but the recurrence and positive margins suggest a more aggressive lesion, and the microscopic examination findings support verrucous carcinoma.

rejected.label: Nasal vestibule squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of recurrence and positive margins, the microscopic examination does not show the typical features of squamous cell carcinoma, such as significant atypia or invasion.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to nasal vestibule squamous cell carcinoma, the microscopic examination does not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's lesion does not show the typical features of basal cell carcinoma, such as a nodular or infiltrative growth pattern.

rejected.label: Inverted papilloma
rejected.why: While inverted papilloma can show a papillomatous growth pattern, the patient's lesion does not show the typical features of inverted papilloma, such as a prominent glandular component or significant mitotic activity.
